title: Check: control plane components
description: Five questions on the API server, etcd, the scheduler and the controller manager.

questions.prompt: Why should an etcd cluster have an odd number of members?

options.text: Raft needs a quorum of (n/2)+1, so an even count adds a member without adding fault tolerance
etcd refuses to start with an even number

questions.explanation: A 2-member cluster is strictly worse than a 1-member one: it tolerates zero failures and has two things that can break.

questions.prompt: The scheduler picks a node in two stages. What are they?

options.text: Filtering out nodes that cannot work, then scoring the survivors
Scoring every node, then asking the kubelet

questions.explanation: Filtering (predicates) eliminates nodes that cannot work; scoring (priorities) ranks what is left. The highest score wins and the scheduler writes a Binding.

questions.prompt: New Pods stay Pending forever, but everything already running is healthy. Which component is down?
questions.explanation: No scheduler means nothing assigns a node, so new Pods never leave Pending. Existing Pods already have a node and are unaffected.

questions.prompt: You delete a Pod belonging to a Deployment and it is never replaced. Which component is down?
questions.explanation: The ReplicaSet controller lives in the controller manager. Without it nothing notices the gap - the cluster simply stops healing itself.

questions.prompt: On a kubeadm cluster, which statements about the control plane are true? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Its components run as static Pods
The kubelet watches that directory and keeps them running
The scheduler decides where to place them

questions.explanation: Static Pods are run straight from disk by the kubelet, with no scheduler involved - which is how the control plane bootstraps the very agent it manages.
